One-sentence judgment: bridge and lock tenders are not "gate watchers"; they operate bridges, locks, and navigation signals according to operating procedures and navigation instructions, control the opening and closing sequence, confirm bridge clearance and lock chamber width, guide vessels through safely, and record vessel and traffic data faithfully. On the U.S. side this corresponds to O*NET-SOC 53-6011.00, listed as Job Zone 1-2 (SVP below 6.0). The core boundary is this: you may operate equipment, issue signals, and record data as authorized, but you may not change the operating plan, the navigation schedule, or structural safety judgments on your own, nor release or operate without confirming clearance, width, and that people have evacuated.

Signals to keep exploring: you are willing to understand the navigation instructions and operating procedures before acting, can stand watch and keep lookout for long periods and accept outdoor and weather exposure; when you find an abnormal vessel attitude, unusual noises from the gate, or a water level or weather beyond the operating conditions, you are willing to stop and report first rather than letting it through; and your interest in "is this release safe and will the record stand up to review" is greater than in "how many vessels I released today".

Before entering the field you can first complete the L1 fictional paper exercise on this page: check the conditions, mark unknown states, and fill in the event record and handover sheet. The exercise is only for experiencing observation, recording, and review; real equipment operation requires separate unit training, assessment, and position authorization.

Education, qualifications, and position authorization must be checked separately: O*NET lists this occupation as Job Zone 1-2, and among respondents 65% think a high school diploma or equivalent is required, 20% think a postsecondary certificate is required, and 15% think less than high school; related work experience and on-the-job training range from a few days to one year. In mainland China, the operating plan for navigation structures should be agreed with and published by the department responsible for waterway management, and the construction or management unit should maintain navigation structures as required and keep them operating normally; the certification, watch duty, and operating authorization for specific positions are determined by the rules of the employing unit and the competent department.

Insufficient evidence: the National Bureau of Statistics 2025 urban unit wage tables consulted this time do not list national wages and employment data for this occupation. The transportation, storage, and postal services average serves only as an industry proxy; wage percentiles, respondent education percentages, and industry employment shares come from the United States and cannot be converted into conclusions about Chinese positions.

The work of this occupation can be divided into three categories: first, standing watch and keeping lookout (confirming equipment and signal status at shift handover, observing the waterway and bridge area, receiving and repeating navigation instructions, and judging vessel types and needs); second, operation and release (operating control levers and valves to open and close gates or bridge spans, confirming that the bridge deck and lock chamber are clear, issuing signals and alarms, guiding vessels into and out of the lock or through the bridge opening, and adjusting operations to the water level); third, recording and maintenance (registering vessel and traffic data, recording water level and weather, reporting abnormalities and accidents, filing maintenance requests, and carrying out daily maintenance such as cleaning, rust removal, touch-up painting, and site tidying). All three share the same traceable chain of operating records.
Standing watch and keeping lookout

Confirm equipment, signal, and communication status at shift handover → observe the waterway and bridge area and identify vessel movements → receive, repeat, and confirm navigation instructions → check whether water level, weather, and visibility are within operating conditions → confirm the release order with the adjacent position or dispatch → record the handover status and outstanding matters.
Operation and release

Confirm that the bridge deck and lock chamber are clear and that people have evacuated → issue signals, navigation lights, and alarms → operate control levers or valves to open and close the bridge span or gate or adjust the water level → guide vessels into and out of the lock or through the bridge opening in order → observe vessel attitude and mooring condition → complete the reset and repeat the confirmation for the next vessel.

Register vessel names, types, and destinations and the number of vehicles or trains crossing the bridge, record water level and weather, register abnormalities and how they were handled, file maintenance requests and follow them to closure, complete cleaning, rust removal, touch-up painting, and site tidying, and hand over equipment status and outstanding problems to the incoming shift.

Bridge and lock tenders center on the operation and release of navigation equipment: security guards are responsible for the security of people and property and do not operate navigation equipment; construction equipment operators (such as excavator or crane operators) are responsible for earthwork and lifting work and do not handle navigation releases; highway maintenance workers maintain the road surface and ancillary facilities and do not control locks or bridge spans; line installers and repairers handle power and communication lines and do not handle navigation signal releases; locksmiths and safe repairers open and repair locks and safes and have nothing to do with navigation equipment. Similar names or working at the same site do not mean responsibilities are interchangeable.
Core purpose

Under conditions that meet navigation requirements and safety requirements, complete bridge span opening and closing and lock releases safely, in order, and in a traceable way, keeping both the waiting time and the risk for vessels and land traffic within the limits allowed by the procedures.
Main objects and basis

The objects are bridge spans, gates, valves, control mechanisms, traffic signals and navigation lights, communication equipment, and the passing subjects such as vessels and vehicles; the basis is the navigation instructions and operating plan, the equipment operating procedures and watch system, the operating limits for water level and weather conditions, and the on-site safe work and protection rules.
Core process

Shift handover confirmation, lookout and identification, instruction receipt and repetition, condition checking, signal issuance, equipment operation, vessel guidance, reset and recording, and abnormality reporting and handover.
Main outputs

The main outputs include bridge or lock operation completed according to the on-site procedures, vessel and vehicle traffic records, water level and weather logs, maintenance work requests, and accident reports; routine facility maintenance and problem reporting are completed according to the actual position duties. These records and work results cannot replace the operating unit's authority to suspend or resume navigation, overhaul, or conduct structural appraisal.
Responsible party

Watch personnel carry out operations and keep true records according to their position duties, and the operating unit is responsible for safe operation; Articles 29—31 of the 2026 measures require qualified education and training, risk inspection, qualified entrusted units, and entrustment contracts. The waterway department approves and supervises the operating plan, while maintenance and periodic safety appraisal are undertaken by the corresponding parties under the rules, and an individual watch inspection does not equal a structural safety appraisal.
Authority and approval

Whether you can open or close, whether you can release, and whether you can continue working in special weather or water levels are determined by the operating plan, the watch system, and on-site instructions; operating authority comes from position authorization and training records and does not arise by itself from proficiency or years of service. Chinese locks and ship lifts are governed by the 2026 amended Measures for the Administration of Navigation Structure Operation: Article 29 requires working only after passing the unit's education and training and clarifying position responsibility; Article 15 requires that adjustments to operating conditions, opening hours, dispatch, and maintenance closures be re-planned and submitted to the original approving department. Bascule bridges and lighthouses cannot be brought directly under these measures merely because the United States groups them in the same occupation.
Boundary of conclusions

The shift record states that "this opening and closing and release were completed according to the procedures and a record was kept"; it does not equal a conclusion on navigation conditions assessment, nor does it replace equipment overhaul or structural safety inspection, and it is affected by visibility, current, equipment condition, and communication conditions.

Before starting the job, check at least six items: the position basis and form of employment (government agency, public institution, or outsourced operation), the watch and shift arrangements, the training and certification requirements, the scope of equipment operating authorization, the reporting and escalation process for abnormalities and accidents, and the real method of pay and work hours.
Occupational basis

The current O*NET 2025 industry distribution: government 82%, transportation and warehousing 16%, other 2%. This describes the industries in which U.S. 53-6011 employment falls, not the staffing shares, income brackets, or employer adoption rates in China. Chinese waterway management, lock operation, bridge management, and outsourced unit positions are checked separately against actual duties, and this round did not verify one-to-one correspondence with detailed category codes.
Education and training path

The O*NET education question asks what education new hires need, and 65% answered high school equivalent, 20% a postsecondary certificate, and 15% below high school, which are position education requirement answers rather than the educational composition of workers. The on-the-job training of a few days to one year for Job Zone1—2 and SVP below 6.0 is a cross-occupation summary; related experience has separate descriptions ranging from none to several months or one year, and they cannot be merged into a fixed period for this occupation. The typical BLS entry for this occupation is a high school equivalent, no related experience, and short-term on-the-job training.
Methods and tools

The Hot Technology page lists six specific products: Excel, Office, Outlook, Word, PeopleSoft, and SAP, and the within-occupation ratios in the 2025 U.S. hiring data are all unpublished; the details page's six software categories additionally include general Email and VPN. The six products and the six categories are different units, and the latter are not all marked Hot; adoption or substitution rates cannot be inferred from the lists.
Safety and work permits

Risks from height, proximity to water, machinery, and traffic require protection, isolation, and communication arrangements chosen according to the equipment and the site; the questionnaire's PPE percentages should not be written as a uniform equipment list. U.S. general industry 1910.22 requires employers to inspect work surfaces and repair or isolate hazards, and structural repairs are performed or supervised by qualified persons; 1910.147 on unexpected startup during servicing has applicable conditions, and an emergency stop button does not equal energy isolation. Chinese locks additionally require checking the operating unit's safety system.
Training and regulatory requirements

In mainland China, the operation and management of waterways and navigation structures is governed by the Waterway Law of the People's Republic of China: the transportation department of the State Council is in charge of national waterway management; the operation of navigation structures should meet the needs of vessel passage, and the operating plan should be agreed with and published by the department responsible for waterway management; the construction or management unit should maintain navigation structures as required and keep them operating normally; the law also prohibits activities in navigation structures, their approach channels, and vessel dispatch areas that affect their normal operation. Chinese locks and ship lifts are governed by the 2026 amended Measures for the Administration of Navigation Structure Operation: Article 29 requires working only after passing the unit's education and training and clarifying position responsibility; Article 15 requires that adjustments to operating conditions, opening hours, dispatch, and maintenance closures be re-planned and submitted to the original approving department. Bascule bridges and lighthouses cannot be brought directly under these measures merely because the United States groups them in the same occupation.
Pay and work hours

Positions are mostly arranged on a watch system by public departments or operating units, with morning, middle, and night shifts and holiday rotation, and overtime may occur with navigation demand; when comparing, put the shift system and rotation rules, night and holiday allowances, peak navigation period arrangements, accommodation and transport arrangements, and who bears training and certification costs into the written agreement.

The U.S. definition covers the operation and tending of bridges, canal locks, and lighthouses, serving vessel passage on inland waterways, coastal waters, and hazardous sections of waterways; it may include supervisory positions. It is not all bridge maintenance personnel, nor vessel pilots, structural safety assessors, or all navigation mark engineers.

O*NET occupational identity and tasks: O*NET-SOC 53-6011.00 Bridge and Lock Tenders, page updated 2026, Job Zone 1-2 (SVP below 6.0), and this occupation is not marked Bright Outlook. The official duties are to "operate and tend bridges, canal locks, and lighthouses to permit the passage of vessels through inland waterways, coastal waters, and hazardous sections of waterways; may supervise such operations; includes drawbridge operators, lock operators, and slip bridge operators"; there are 18 tasks in total, and the highly important tasks include operating mechanisms to open and close locks, dams, and drawbridges (98), directing vessel movement using signals and communication equipment (96), observing vessel position and progress (96), registering vessel names, types, destinations, and bridge crossing counts (92), and watching for approaching vessels and recognizing whistle signals (91). The 18 tasks comprise 10 Core and 8 Supplemental. Among the latter, using valves to adjust water levels (100), clearing the bridge deck (98), and stopping traffic (96) must not be overlooked merely because they are not Core. There are also 13 detailed activities; 41 is the number of general activities.

U.S. wage distribution: the 2025 BLS Occupational Employment and Wage Statistics (OEWS) presented by O*NET, on the basis of Bridge and Lock Tenders (SOC 53-6011) — annual wage 10th percentile 28,090 USD, 25th percentile 38,640 USD, median 57,700 USD, 75th percentile 69,620 USD, and 90th percentile 75,360 USD; the corresponding hourly wage is 13.51 USD at the 10th percentile, 27.74 USD at the median, and 36.23 USD at the 90th percentile.

Mainland China side: the National Bureau of Statistics "Average Annual Wages of Urban Unit Employees in 2025" (published 2026-05-15) publishes average wages by industry sector and broad position category but does not list the occupation "bridge and lock tenders" separately; following the evidence routing, this page publishes only the transportation, storage, and postal services (urban non-private units) industry average of 133,981 yuan per year as an explicit proxy, and makes clear that it is not this occupation's occupational wage. The same release also gives transportation private 73133 and public facilities non-private 70172 yuan per year, both only industry references with different coverage.

paragraphs: This page compares bridge and lock tenders with five adjacent directions on the same set of dimensions: career direction, core work and output, key differences, and which direction suits each preference. The adjacent directions are described according to their own official occupational descriptions and do not mean the trade names are interchangeable.

Evidence note: the career directions and core outputs are based on the official descriptions of O*NET 53-6011.00 and adjacent occupations and are on the U.S. basis; the qualification, licensing, and safety requirements of adjacent trades must be verified separately by their own jurisdiction, and this page does not present any direction as a shortcut to a career change.

The table below compares bridge and lock tenders with adjacent trades and the paths for moving in from adjacent positions; the basis for judgment is the main output, what the role is responsible for, and the training required, rather than how similar the trade names are.
Security Guards (33-9032.00)
Responsible for the security of people, property, and premises and for access control, with patrol records and incident handling as the main output.

Both have watch duty and record keeping as the norm; but security work is about the safety of people and premises, whereas bridge and lock tenders operate navigation equipment and vessel passage and must control machinery and signals according to operating procedures.
If you would rather do security work for people and premises, look first at security guards; if you would rather operate navigation equipment and guide vessels, look first at bridge and lock tenders.
Operating Engineers (47-2073.00)
Operate construction machinery for excavation, lifting, and earthwork, with earthwork, lifting, and foundation results as the main output.

Construction equipment operation is part of the engineering construction chain, with machinery capability and work face conditions at the core; bridge and lock tenders center on scheduled opening and closing and passage order and cannot change the navigation sequence on their own.

If you would rather operate large machinery to complete engineering work, look first at operating engineers; if you would rather stand watch according to procedures and ensure navigation, look first at bridge and lock tenders.
Highway Maintenance Workers (47-4051.00)
Maintain the road surface, shoulders, and ancillary facilities and organize traffic during work, with properly maintained road facilities as the main output.

Highway maintenance takes road facilities as its object and often works in an open traffic environment; bridge and lock tenders take navigation structures and their operating condition as their object and must attend to both waterway and land passage.

If you would rather do road facility maintenance and traffic organization, look first at highway maintenance workers; if you would rather do watch duty on navigation equipment, look first at bridge and lock tenders.
Line Installers and Repairers (electric power 49-9051; telecommunications 49-9052)
Install and repair power and communication lines, with safely operating lines and facilities as the main output.

Line installation and repair is a collective term for adjacent directions: 49-9051.00 refers to power line installation and repair, and telecommunications lines are 49-9052.00, and they cannot be merged into the same detailed category. Both handle lines and equipment and do not handle navigation releases for locks or bridge spans; specific electrical and work-at-height qualifications must be checked separately.

If you would rather do line installation and repair, look first at line installers and repairers; if you would rather do watch duty and releases on navigation equipment, look first at bridge and lock tenders.
Locksmiths and Safe Repairers (49-9094.00)
Open, replace, and repair locks and safes, with properly functioning lock systems as the main output.
Locksmith work centers on the repair technique of mechanical and electronic locks; bridge and lock tenders do not repair locks but operate navigation machinery according to procedures.

If you would rather do technical work on locks and security hardware, look first at locksmiths and safe repairers; if you would rather do navigation watch duty and machinery operation, look first at bridge and lock tenders.
Moving in from an adjacent position or labor employment
You already have watch duty, gatekeeping, port and navigation assistance, or construction assistance experience and want to move to standardized navigation equipment operation positions.

The gap is usually not physical strength but navigation procedures and instruction repetition, equipment operation and signal issuance, judging water level and weather conditions, vessel guidance and record standards, and the abnormality escalation process; having watched from the bridge head or the lock side does not mean you can stand watch independently.

If you are willing to start from an assistant position and accept mentoring and assessment, you can consider moving in; if you only want to press buttons without learning the procedures and abnormality handling, the gap will be large.

Conclusion: the basis for choosing a direction is the main output, what the role is responsible for, and the training required, not how similar the names are; once the direction is set, check the target position's operating procedures and certification requirements, the actual duty and shift arrangements, the protection arrangements for work near water and at height, and the form of employment and settlement method item by item, and keep written confirmation.

paragraphs: Students or career changers preparing to enter this occupation

Students or career changers should first complete the L1 paper condition check and handover record on this page, then check the target unit's training, position authorization, and shift system. The paper experience can be completed without a site or a mentor; it does not constitute proof of equipment operating ability.
Practicing bridge and lock tenders

Editorial suggestion: use digital tools in reviewable links such as traffic record keeping and statistics, organizing water level and weather data, equipment status and shift ledgers, and maintenance work order flow; lookout judgment, equipment operation, signal issuance, vessel guidance, and abnormality handling must still rest with people.
Operating units and waterway management departments

Editorial suggestion: before introducing tools, clarify the links where they may be used, the knowledge scope for traffic and equipment data, the written basis for the operating plan and watch system, and the responsible person for recording and review, so that any output returns to traceable operating records and equipment ledgers.
Education and development

Editorial suggestion: focus training on navigation procedures and instruction repetition, equipment operation and signal issuance, judging water level and weather conditions, vessel guidance and mooring observation, and abnormality and accident reporting, and also train the habit of checking tool output.

Digital tools can assist with records, ledgers, and work orders, and equipment automation may also change some control and monitoring tasks. Direct answer: the main risks include falls from height and into water, mechanical opening and pinching injuries, conflicts with land vehicles and pedestrians, declining attention from long watch periods, outdoor weather and cold or heat exposure, and passage accidents caused by operating without following the operating plan and instructions; control depends on the operating plan and watch system, signal and isolation measures, personal protection, and the abnormality reporting and escalation process.

items.title: What evidence employers usually look at

values: L1 fictional paper record pack

The L1 fictional paper record pack uses only pen and paper or a local spreadsheet and takes about 60—90 minutes; no equipment, site, PPE, mentor, or additional materials are needed. The following values are all editorial settings and are not any real bridge or lock standard.

L1 rules: vessel width ≤8 m and vessel height ≤5 m; water level 1.8—2.4 m (endpoints included); visibility ≥500 m; the three conditions of normal equipment, cleared area, and clear communication must all be explicitly confirmed. Meeting all of them can only be recorded as "simulated conditions complete", not a release. Any over-limit item or communication failure is recorded as "pause and report"; any unknown is recorded as "to be confirmed", and an unknown must not be filled in as normal.

Input six events: 08:00 A (width 7, height 4, water 2.0, visibility 600; equipment normal, area cleared, communication clear); 08:10 B (width 9, height 4, water 2.0, visibility 600, the rest confirmed); 08:20 C (width 8, height 5, water 2.4, visibility 500; equipment unknown, area cleared, communication clear); 08:30 C (same values; equipment confirmed normal, area unknown, communication clear); 08:40 C (same values; all three confirmed); 08:50 A (same dimensions, water level, and visibility as 08:00; communication failed, the rest confirmed). All lengths in m, visibility in m, and the times within the same fictional shift.

Handover materials: D1 is the problem statement version for L1, and D2 is an additional illustration version marked "not confirmed"; the exercise does not need D2 to check the problem statement, but D2 must not be written as matched. The record fields are fixed as time, vessel ID, input conditions, judgment, reason, and next step; unknown items keep the original text.
What must be submitted
Make a L1 condition check table and write the judgment and basis for the six events row by row; boundaries equal to the threshold are judged by the rules, and no extra safety margin may be invented.
Write three abnormality or missing-item records and distinguish over-limit, unknown, and communication failure; explain why a later correction cannot overwrite the old record.

Prepare a handover sheet: list this shift's six events, the number of different vessels involved, the final status, and the unconfirmed D2 version item; count the number of events with "simulated conditions complete" and the number of different vessels separately.
Reference answer and item-by-item self-check

Reference answer: 08:00 A simulated conditions complete; 08:10 B pause and report (9>8 width over the limit); 08:20 C to be confirmed (equipment unknown; 8=8, 5=5, 2.4=the upper limit, and 500=the lower limit all meet the numerical conditions).

08:30 C is still to be confirmed (equipment being confirmed does not mean the area is also confirmed); 08:40 C simulated conditions complete; 08:50 A pause and report (communication failure), and the old 08:00 status must not be carried over.

The abnormality list must cover at least B's width over-limit, C's two different unknown fields, and A's communication failure; keep all the old time points. Handover: six events and three different vessels A/B/C; 2 complete events (08:00 A and 08:40 C) involving 2 vessels. Final status A paused, B paused, C complete; the D2 version is not confirmed, and the missing item must still be retained.

Self-check: recalculate from the input from the beginning and check units, equals signs, unknowns, and times cell by cell; check the counts 6 events / 3 vessels / 2 complete events / 2 complete vessels and do not mistake the event count for the vessel count. No external expert signature is needed; keep your own wrong items and the reasons for correction.
Boundaries between the exercise and real authority

L1 is only a paper record and condition logic exercise; it does not give real gate, valve, light signal, whistle, waterway clearance, or current operating procedures. These thresholds or the "complete" label must not be used to guide real releases, equipment control, or accident judgments.

Do not enter real near-water, height, or operating facilities, do not issue real signals, and do not pretend to have authorization or training experience; real safety measures and decisions must be based on the facility's procedures, position training, on-site checking, and the authorization chain.
L1 condition check table

L1 check table: list the values, the three statuses, the judgment, and the reason for each of the six events cell by cell; write "fictional paper exercise, not on-site operation" at the top of the page.
List conditions complete, records complete, and individual authorization separately; write the D2 version as unconfirmed and do not guess to fill it in.
Independent self-check record

Self-check record: cover the reference answer and judge row by row first, then check 6 events / 3 vessels / 2 complete events / 2 complete vessels; keep the errors, the reasons for correction, and the date.
External watch personnel opinions are optional and are not a precondition for completing the paper exercise.
Handover review

Handover review: list the final status of A/B/C, the different times when C's equipment and area were unknown, A's communication failure, and the unconfirmed D2 version; explain that a later confirmation does not erase the earlier unknown.
A one-page deliverable only proves the exercise process and cannot be written as a real safety release, an on-site record, or a unit assessment certificate.
Tool use note
Tool note: pen and paper may be used with no software threshold; when using a spreadsheet, note the file version, formulas, and manual review method.
Keep the original input and the time order; judgments generated by a template must be checked cell by cell, and real operating or vessel data must not be uploaded.

entries.answer: Stand watch according to operating procedures and navigation instructions: observe the waterway and bridge area, receive and repeat instructions, confirm water level and weather conditions, operate control levers or valves to open and close bridge spans and gates, issue signals and alarms, guide vessels into and out of the lock or through the bridge opening, and register vessel and traffic data, water level, and weather, report abnormalities and accidents, and complete cleaning and site tidying.
entries.question: What do bridge and lock tenders do every day?

entries.answer: The risks to watch for in advance include falls from height and into water, mechanical opening and pinching injuries, conflicts with land vehicles and pedestrians, declining attention from long watch periods, and passage accidents caused by operating without following the operating plan and instructions; control depends on the operating plan, signal and isolation measures, personal protection, and the abnormality reporting and escalation process.

entries.answer: Fit signals are maintaining attention during long watch periods, repeating instructions accurately and operating equipment according to procedures, and stopping and reporting first when conditions do not meet requirements or the equipment is abnormal; an interest in machinery or the waterfront environment alone is not enough to prove competence.

source_links.scope: The lock operating unit implements the approved plan, maintenance patrols, and the responsibility system; Article 22 prohibits vessels not meeting the stated standards from passing through the lock, and Article 34 lists the conditions for suspending opening and the publication and reporting of navigation suspension and resumption information. Personnel report and handle matters according to their own position's procedures and cannot set operating conditions or resume navigation on the basis of a personal checklist.

Before opening or closing the bridge span, confirm that vehicles and pedestrians have left and implement the stop signals according to that bridge's operating procedures. Locks check vessel and lock chamber conditions under their own procedures; U.S. general industry 1910.147 on servicing involving unexpected startup requires checking its scope separately, an emergency stop button is not an energy isolation device, and stopping the machine does not mean you may enter a pinch area.

Choose near-water, height, and machinery protection according to the site risk assessment, facility procedures, and training. U.S. general industry 1910.22 requires employers to provide safe access and to inspect and repair or isolate hazardous work surfaces, and structural repairs are performed or supervised by a qualified person; an individual patrol does not constitute a structural appraisal, and Chinese requirements must be checked separately.
